input.question: What was the design decision for KRaft timeout-metrics as of 2026-05-14 regarding whether fetch/election timeout count metrics should always report a value regardless of node epoch state or should be registered/unregistered based on state?

content.content: {"result":"{\"answer\":\"Based on the context filesystem, I found the design decision for KIP-1322 (KRaft timeout metrics) as of 2026-05-14.\\n\\n## Answer\\n\\n**The design decision was: Always report metrics, increment counter only on expiration.**\\n\\nThis is documented in **`/store/window-118-summary.md`** (lines 161-165) under the \\\"Mailing List Activity\\\" section covering KIP discussions active during the window of 2026-05-14:\\n\\n> **KIP-1322** (Kraft Metrics): Fetch timeouts and election timeouts metrics\\n> - Detailed discussion about metric registration/unregistration across state transitions\\n> - Discussion between Tony Tang and Kevin Wu on implementation details\\n> - Focus: Always report metrics vs. conditional reporting\\n> - **Resolution approach: Always report metrics, increment counter only on expiration**\\n\\nThis design decision resolves the question of whether fetch/election timeout count metrics should be registered/unregistered based on node epoch state (conditional reporting) or should always report a value. {"answer":"Based on the context filesystem, I found the design decision for KIP-1322 (KRaft timeout metrics) as of 2026-05-14.

## Answer

**The design decision was: Always report metrics, increment counter only on expiration.**

This is documented in **`/store/window-118-summary.md`** (lines 161-165) under the "Mailing List Activity" section covering KIP discussions active during the window of 2026-05-14:

> **KIP-1322** (Kraft Metrics): Fetch timeouts and election timeouts metrics
> - Detailed discussion about metric registration/unregistration across state transitions
> - Discussion between Tony Tang and Kevin Wu on implementation details
> - Focus: Always report metrics vs. conditional reporting
> - **Resolution approach: Always report metrics, increment counter only on expiration**

This design decision resolves the question of whether fetch/election timeout count metrics should be registered/unregistered based on node epoch state (conditional reporting) or should always report a value. The resolution was to **always report the metrics** (ensuring they're always present regardless of node epoch state), but only **increment the counter when the timeout actually expires** (conditional counting).","error":null,"files":["store","window-118-summary.md","mailing-list/window-119-kip-discussions.md","kips-and-discussions.md","mailing-list/window-117-kip-discussions.md","discussions/mailing-list-threads.md","jira-issues/window-118-issues-index.md","window-114-summary.md","window-125-summary.md"],"seconds":61.68,"truncated":false,"turns":1,"usage":{"cache_read_tokens":624904,"cache_write_tokens":39408,"cost_usd":0.1649064,"input_tokens":210,"output_tokens":4678}}
